extracted.intended_audience: principal investigators, grant reviewers, and molecular biology researchers working on protein–RNA interactions and innate immunity (OAS1/RNase L)
extracted.subtask_short: writing an NIH-style molecular biology grant
extracted.subtask_description: A research strategy / Specific Aims section for an NIH-style grant proposing mechanistic experiments (in vitro, cellular, biophysical, structural) to define how dsRNA features control activation of OAS1. Focus is on experimental design, rigor, controls, and alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear Specific Aims with explicit hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims should state precise experimental goals and an explicit hypothesis (e.g., Aim 1: define dsRNA features and context that lead to potent OAS1 activation; Hypothesis: extent of OAS1 activation is determined by context of overlapping RNA features; Aim 2: determine molecular mechanisms by which non-activating and hyper-activating dsRNAs differ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims should summarize planned experiments and link to hypothesis-driven questions; include brief rationale and how aims complement each other (summary figure referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological significance and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe why the question matters for biology/medicine (e.g., understanding dsRNA regulation of OAS1 is critical to host-pathogen interactions and antiviral therapeutic development).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect mechanistic findings to broader impacts (how viruses might evade OAS1/RNase L; translational potential).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum dsRNA length requirement for OAS1 binding/activation
rubrics_metrics.description: OAS1 requires double-stranded regions with a minimum length of 18 base pairs for RNA binding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design constructs to meet this requirement; justify hairpin length choices to avoid off-target dsRNA sensor activation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Known activating RNA motifs to include/assess
rubrics_metrics.description: Activation is potentiated by activating consensus sequences (e.g., WWN9WG) and the 3'-end single-stranded pyrimidine (3'-ssPy) motif that the lab identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test how these motifs and their context (position/orientation/overlap) alter activation; include variants/mutations targeting these motifs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of established in vitro enzymatic assay to measure OAS1 activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure OAS1 enzyme kinetics in vitro using a chromogenic assay that detects inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi) produced during 2'-5'-oligoadenylate synthesis (absorbance at 580 nm after ammonium molybdate reagent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform assays across a range of RNA concentrations to determine kinetic parameters (Vmax and Kapp) using Michaelis-Menten fits; include raw assay details (96-well plate format, plate reader).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include appropriate positive and negative controls in biochemical assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Controls listed include ATP degradation (no OAS1), no RNA (negative), poly(rI:rC) dsRNA (positive), wild-type and scrambled dsRNA hairpins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include these controls on each plate to monitor assay performance and background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition assays to test binding-site competition model
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform competition experiments with fixed hyper-activating dsRNA and titrated non-activating dsRNA to test if non-activating RNA can compete for OAS1 binding in trans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design competition assays to directly probe productive vs non-productive binding sites and interpret effects on enzyme kinetics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical replicates and prep-to-prep reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Each experiment should be performed in three technical replicates and use at least two different preps of recombinant OAS1 to assess prep-to-prep variability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include internal standards (poly(rI:rC), wild-type) on each plate to control for prep variability; average data and report standard error/standard deviation as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data processing and kinetic analysis standards
rubrics_metrics.description: After background correction, convert absorbance to nmol PPi via a PPi standard curve; fit curves using non-linear regression to obtain Vmax and Kapp using the Michaelis-Menten model Y=(Vmax X)/(Kapp+X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use GraphPad Prism for plotting and non-linear regression; clearly report fit methods and parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell-based assay design to validate in vitro findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfect dsRNA hairpins into A549 cells and measure OAS/RNase L activity by RT-ddPCR for known RNase L targets (FAT4, FREM2, PCDHB5, ZEB1) and by assessing rRNA cleavage on agarose gels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use A549 cells (express OAS1 without interferon stimulation) to reduce complexity; include time points (example: 1 and 3 hours post-transfection) and appropriate transfection controls (mock, poly(rI:rC), scramble RNAs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of RT-ddPCR for sensitive and absolute quantification
rubrics_metrics.description: RT-ddPCR is preferred to detect small differences and minor species and allows absolute cDNA copy number quantification without a standard curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-determine cell number for back calculation of transcripts per cell; pair with rRNA cleavage assays to capture weak and robust activation gradients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological replicates and statistical testing for cellular data
rubrics_metrics.description: Cellular experiments will be performed in biological triplicates; data plotted with GraphPad Prism and statistical significance determined using unpaired Student’s t-test (p<0.05).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report standard deviation for biological replicates; choose appropriate tests for comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for potential pitfalls and alternative approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate technique-specific pitfalls and provide alternatives (e.g., if chromogenic assay problematic, use [α32P]-ATP incorporation; for ddPCR issues use qRT-PCR; if agarose gel inconclusive use Bioanalyzer; if off-target sensors activated use knockout cell lines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly list feasible alternatives and resources (e.g., cores, knockout lines) to demonstrate technical feasibility and robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design constructs to minimize activation of other dsRNA sensors
rubrics_metrics.description: Use short dsRNA hairpins to simplify preparation, ease transfection, and reduce activation of other dsRNA sensors (e.g., PKR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If other sensors are activated, use knockout cell lines or redesign constructs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biophysical binding studies (BLI) with rigorous controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure dsRNA binding affinity (Kd) and kinetics (kon, koff) using bio-layer interferometry with OAS1-AviTag immobilized on streptavidin biosensors; include reference sensors and biocytin/background corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize buffer conditions, loading density, analyte concentration, molecule orientation; run technical replicates and use at least two independent protein preps; subtract reference sensor signal in analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay optimization parameters must be documented and tested
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize parameters such as buffer composition, OAS1/dsRNA concentrations, molecule orientation, loading density, and reference sensors for each biophysical assay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify no preferred orientation by also testing immobilized biotinylated dsRNA if feasible; document optimization steps and choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: HDX-MS experimental design and coverage standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry with comprehensive peptide mapping (example: 100% OAS1 sequence coverage, 33-fold redundancy), multiple time points (e.g., 0, 15, 60, 180, 600 s), duplicate experiments with independent preps, and multiple injections for redundancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in-line pepsin digestion, calculate differential deuterium uptake (apo vs each dsRNA), map onto structure; analyze with Masslynx, PLGS, Dynamix; ensure high redundancy (e.g., six injections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure determination and validation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain crystals, optimize conditions, collect diffraction data at a beamline (e.g., SER-CAT), determine structures by molecular replacement (using PDB 4IG8), refine and validate using HKL2000, Phenix, Coot, and final validation with PDB server.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document crystallization optimization steps (salt, precipitant, pH, temperature, additives); validate structures during refinement and deposit-quality checks before interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking biochemistry, biophysics, and structure to mechanistic interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate enzyme kinetics, cellular assays, binding kinetics, HDX-MS, and crystal structures to define molecular mechanisms by which different dsRNAs modulate OAS1 activity (e.g., affinity vs kinetics vs induced conformational changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State expected outcomes and alternative interpretations; if data do not support one mechanism (e.g., no affinity differences), pivot to other approaches (protein dynamics, structural analyses) as planned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of preliminary data to demonstrate feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Include preliminary biochemical, BLI, HDX-MS, and crystallization data showing feasibility (e.g., OAS1-AviTag is biotinylated and active; preliminary BLI shows binding; HDX-MS mapping achieved 100% coverage; crystals diffract to ~7 Å).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage preliminary results to justify methods and timelines; reference figures/letters from cores where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized reporting of experimental outcomes and interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: For each subaim, describe expected observations, how results will be interpreted mechanistically (examples provided), and what follow-up experiments would be done based on outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state possible outcomes (e.g., changes in Vmax or Kapp; differences in kon/koff; HDX differences) and the downstream experiments (mutagenesis, functional assays) to test hypotheses generated by those outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of established molecular biology protocols for construct and reagent preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: In vitro transcribe dsRNA from linearized plasmid templates using T7 RNA polymerase and purify RNAs by denaturing PAGE; express human OAS1 in E. coli and purify via Ni2+-affinity, heparin-affinity, and gel filtration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite and follow established protocols (references provided) and maintain QC across preps; include scramble controls with defined sequence randomization strategies.
